description: Normative crosswalk from the Advisor's normalizedProfile to the prerequisite skill's question fields. The consumer is told not to ask again for a fact the Advisor already established, but the two skills name and type their facts differently, so without this table the rule cannot be implemented deterministically: two implementations reading the same handoff would disagree about which questions are already answered. Every entry states what converts, what does not, and what the consumer may claim as a result. Enforced by tests/check-prerequisite-skill.mjs. The field below is `mappingsVersion` and not `version`: a bare version on a bundle file reads as a claim about the coordinated schema and knowledge base lines, which the startup check compares and halts on, so a healthy crosswalk with its own release history could stop a run for disagreeing with lines it was never declaring.

conversionKinds.direct: The value carries over unchanged, or through a documented label-to-ID mapping.
conversionKinds.vocabulary: The value carries over but the allowed values differ and must be translated.
conversionKinds.not-convertible: The producer value cannot establish the consumer field. The consumer must still ask. Stating why is the point of the entry: a qualitative answer is not a measurement, and a partial list is not an inventory.

Same vocabulary on both sides. This entry was missing while both skills carried the field: the Advisor typed it in v3.11.0, questions.json has fed P03-001 and P09-001 with it since the catalog shipped, and the crosswalk between them named neither, so a handoff dropped the fact and the consumer asked again for something it had been told. The per-consumer effects matter here and are questions.json's business, not this table's: P03-001 accepts BULK_LOGGED for log shipping and P09-001 does not.

Asymmetric on purpose, because the two directions are not equally conclusive. A reported break is proof of a problem and converts to MISSING, which makes the prerequisite a blocker. A reported intact chain is not proof of restore readiness and converts to nothing: `backup_chain_status` feeds eight blocking rows whose evidence columns ask for `RESTORE VERIFYONLY`, a gap check and a restore rehearsal, and the consumer is told not to re-ask an inherited fact, so mapping intact to CONFIRMED cleared all eight on one sentence from the user and moved a never-tested restore route off `blocked`. This entry shipped that way for one release. An intact chain is an input to proof, not the proof.
Same vocabulary on both sides, so it carries over without translation.

The Advisor records what the user said about ports; the consumer records a status. Only an explicit confirmation converts to CONFIRMED. Free text that merely fails to mention a block is not a confirmation. The emitted value is the consumer's own vocabulary: blocked ports are MISSING, which makes the prerequisite a blocker, and anything else is UNKNOWN. This side used to emit MI_LINK_PORTS_CONFIRMED and lowercase unknown, neither of which questions.json accepts, so a confirmed answer became unknown and blocked ports never became a blocker.

Renamed and re-vocabularised. The Advisor asks whether the backup can actually reach Blob storage over HTTPS; the consumer records that reachability as a status. Only an explicit confirmation converts to CONFIRMED, because an unverified upload path is unknown rather than working: a real session reported a backup gate as passed with the Blob path never tested. A stated block converts to MISSING, which makes the prerequisite a blocker, and everything else stays UNKNOWN.

The Advisor holds a size band chosen from a menu; the consumer needs a number in gigabytes. A band cannot be turned into a measurement without inventing precision the user never gave. The consumer asks, and the band may be offered as the default range.

A qualitative statement about performance is not evidence that a baseline was captured. Treating it as one would let 'the workload is bursty' satisfy a prerequisite asking for measured log-rate and latency figures.
A list of dependencies the user happened to mention is not proof that an inventory was run. The distinction matters because the prerequisite exists to catch the dependency nobody thought of.

The Advisor's ports field is free text about specific ports. The consumer's field is a status covering the whole network path, including DNS and private endpoints. A statement about one port does not establish the path.
A region name means the same thing on both sides, and the consumer's field records nothing more than which region was named. Asking twice would be asking the user to repeat themselves.

The Advisor records the recovery point the business needs. The consumer records whether the selected method meets it, which is why its values are compatible, incompatible and unknown rather than a duration. A requirement is not a verdict on the method chosen to satisfy it, so the stated figure carries into the question as context and the question is still asked.

Same shape as rpo. The Advisor holds the recovery time the business needs; the consumer holds whether the cutover and rollback plan can deliver it. The two are only equal once someone has checked, and checking is the prerequisite.

The Advisor holds the services the user named: SSIS, SSRS, jobs, logins, whatever came up in conversation. The consumer holds whether an inventory of instance-level objects was actually run. A list someone recalled is not a list someone produced, and the prerequisite exists for the object nobody remembered. The named services carry into the question as a starting point, never as the answer.
